key_insight: The paper reports the first bulk synthesis of phase-pure Cs2AgBiI6, enabled by removing trace moisture and using halide exchange from Cs2AgBiBr6.
engineering_relevance: This opens a lead-free iodide double-perovskite absorber candidate for solar and optoelectronic devices, with demonstrated film growth and photoconductive response.
method: Prepared Cs2AgBiI6 microcrystals by anion exchange from phase-pure Cs2AgBiBr6
Eliminated trace moisture to achieve complete halide exchange and phase purity
Formed phase-pure films by flash thermal evaporation of Cs2AgBiBr6 followed by anion exchange
evidence_signal: The product showed broad visible absorption with a 1.70 ± 0.05 eV bandgap, near-IR photoluminescence at 1.03 eV, long-term room-temperature stability, and measurable photoconductivity in films.
watch_item: The material is stabilized only under dry/inert conditions, so moisture control during synthesis and processing remains critical.
paper_title: Synthesis of the Elusive Bulk Iodide Double-Perovskite Semiconductor, Cs2AgBiI6: Microcrystals and Photoconductive Films
